entities.summary: Air Vice Marshal Allan Leslie Walters, CB, CBE, AFC was a senior commander in the Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF). Born in Victoria and raised in Western Australia, he graduated from the Royal Military College, Duntroon, before transferring to the RAAF in 1928. He was one of the service's leading flying instructors and aerobatic pilots between the wars, and was appointed to his first squadron command in 1937. Over the course of World War II, Walters led No. 1 Squadron in Singapore, No. 1 (Fighter) Wing in Darwin, Northern Territory, No. 72 Wing in Dutch New Guinea, and Northern Command in Papua New Guinea.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a senior commander in the Royal Australian Air Force during World War II, Air Vice Marshal Allan Walters played a crucial role in leading No. 1 Squadron in Singapore and No. 72 Wing in Dutch New Guinea, contributing to the Allied victory in the Pacific Theater.
